[[File:View along Manzhou Beach.jpg|thumb|View along Mazhou Beach, located near [[Feliru]], [[Heiso]]]]
'''Crisqui''' is a historical [[Wikipedia:region|region]] in [[North Ayuma]] and [[north Acrola]] encompassing the entirety of present-day [[Heiso]], parts of the modern-day [[Estijan]] and the minor parts of [[Areoix Lie]]. The exact geographical extent varies depending on the definition: in the narrow sense, the area constituted by (excluding Heiso) the Arten provinces of [[Outer Heanuin]], and [[Inner Heanuin]], Estijan state [[Estijan Crisqui]]; The parts of Crisqui ceded to Estijan are collectively known as [[Northern Crisqui]] or Estijan Crisqui. 

The name ''Crisqui'' is an [[endonym and exonym|exonym]] (derived from the endonym "[[Crisqui people|Crisqui]]" of an independent [[Crisqui language|Crisqui]] origin. The history of "Crisqui" (''Crisqie'') as a [[Toponymy|toponym]] in Areoix Lie is disputed, with some scholars believing it was never used while others believe it was by the late 15th century. The area was historically known by various names in Areoix Lie, such as ''Heiso'' (north of the [[Lohanu Pass|Pass]]) or the ''Fifth Province,'' reflecting its semi-independent status under the many Arten dynasties. ''Crisqui'' as a geographical term was first used in the 15th or 16th centuries by Estijan before spreading to [[Ayuma]] and [[Acrola]]. The term was promoted by the [[Estijan Huan]] to separate it from its Arten connections. Although the toponym is still used, some scholars treat the term with caution or avoid it altogether due to its association with [[Estijan colonial empire|Estijan colonialism]]. The ''Fifth Province'' and the ''Southeast'' were also in concurrent use among the Estijan along with ''Crisqui'' until the [[Mivlo incident]] of ____.
